author: Adelaar, K. A.
title: Reconstruction of Proto-Batak phonology
notes: Consulted directly on 25 November 2026 (a 20-page scan in Downloads, no title page; volume details as commonly cited). Six dialects: Karo, Dairi (Northern Batak), Toba, Angkola, Mandailing (Southern Batak) and Simalungun; Alas excluded for lack of data (p. 1). Part I gives each dialect's phoneme system and morphophonology from the written language and dictionaries (Neumann for Karo, the Dairi-Pakpak dictionary, van der Tuuk and Warneck for Toba, Eggink for Angkola-Mandailing, Saragih and Tarigan for Simalungun); Part II the PB vowels *a, *e, *i, *u, *ow, *uy, *ey and consonants *b, *d, *g, *j, *p, *t, *k, *c, *h, *m, *n, *ŋ, *r, *l, *s, *w, *y (PB lexical reconstructions numbered 1-136); §11 (p. 17) the tree: Proto-Batak > Proto-Northern-Batak (Karo, Dairi, Alas?) and Proto-Southern-Batak (Simalungun, Proto-Toba > Toba, Proto-Angkola-Mandailing > Angkola, Mandailing); Part III the PB system against PAN (§§12-14, pp. 17-18). Two asterisks mark PB etyma, two crosses loans; shwa is written ə.
